{{Short description|American statistician}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=April 2022}}
'''Simon J. Sheather''' is an Australian-American academic. He became the 8th dean of the [[University of Kentucky]]’s [[Gatton College of Business and Economics]] on July 1st, 2018.<ref>{{cite news |last1=McCarroll |first1=Peyton |title=New dean named for Gatton College of Business and Economics |url=http://www.kykernel.com/news/new-dean-named-for-gatton-college-of-business-and-economics/article_01125f66-6681-11e8-a850-cf5ebaaeeff6.html |access-date=3 September 2021 |agency=Kentucky Kernel |issue=2 June 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=UK names new dean of Gatton College of Business and Economics |url=https://www.lanereport.com/101768/2018/05/uk-names-new-dean-of-gatton-college-of-business-and-economics/ |access-date=3 September 2021 |work=The Lane Report |date=31 May 2018}}</ref> A Fellow of the [[American Statistical Association]], Sheather is known for the Sheather-Jones bandwidth selection method for [[kernel density estimation]].<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Sheather |first1=Simon J. |title="A reliable data-based bandwidth selection method for kernel density estimation". |journal=Journal of the Royal Statistical Society, Series |date=1991 |volume=53 |issue=3 |pages=683–690 |doi=10.1111/j.2517-6161.1991.tb01857.x |url=https://rss.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/j.2517-6161.1991.tb01857.x|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

==Early life and education==
Sheather was born and raised in Australia, the son of a bank clerk and a nurse.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Sheather |first1=Simon |title=Biography: The Life of Margaret Sheather |url=https://mays.tamu.edu/ms-analytics/biography/ |website=Mays Business School MS Analytics |publisher=Texas A&M University |access-date=1 November 2021}}</ref> Sheather graduated with 1st Class Honours in mathematical statistics from the [[University of Melbourne]] and earned his Ph.D. in statistics from [[La Trobe University]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Faculty Profile: Simon Sheather |url=https://gatton.uky.edu/faculty-research/faculty/sheather-simon |website=Gatton College of Business and Economics |publisher=University of Kentucky |access-date=3 September 2021}}</ref>

==Career==
His academic career includes professorships at the [[University of New South Wales]] and Texas A&M University as well as visiting professorships at Pennsylvania State University and the Stern School of Business at [[New York University]].<ref>{{cite news |title=New Dean Named for UK's Gatton College of Business and Economics |url=https://smileypete.com/business/gatton-college-new-dean/ |access-date=3 September 2021 |publisher=Smiley Pete Publishing |date=31 May 2018}}</ref> While at Texas A&M, he started two professional master’s programs.

In 2021, Sheather was named as the first holder of the Truist Chair in Data Analytics.<ref>{{cite web |last1=McDonald |first1=Diane |title=Dean Simon Sheather Named 1st Endowed Truist Chair in Data Analytics |url=https://uknow.uky.edu/professional-news/dean-simon-sheather-named-1st-endowed-truist-chair-data-analytics |website=University of Kentucky |date=17 March 2021 |access-date=3 September 2021}}</ref>

==Selected works==
* Simon, Sheather (2009), A Modern Approach to Regression with R, Springer<ref>{{cite book |last1=Sheather |first1=Simon |title=A Modern Approach to Regression with R |date=2009 |publisher=Springer |isbn=978-0-387-09608-7 |url=https://www.springer.com/gp/book/9780387096070}}</ref>
* Sheather, S.J.; Jones, M.C. (1991). "A reliable data-based bandwidth selection method for kernel density estimation". Journal of the Royal Statistical Society, Series B. 53 (3): 683–690. doi:10.1111/j.2517-6161.1991.tb01857.x. [https://rss.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/j.2517-6161.1991.tb01857.x JSTOR 2345597].

==Recognition==
Sheather was named a Fellow of the American Statistical Association in 2001.<ref>{{cite web |title=Fellows of the ASA |url=https://www.amstat.org/ASA/Your-Career/Awards/ASA-Fellows-list.aspx |website=American Statistical Association |publisher=American Statistical Association |access-date=1 November 2021}}</ref>
